# Opening Case: Did Christ Have a Biological Father?

**Position.** No. Jesus had a mother, Mary, but no human male who begat him. His conception was the work of the Holy Ghost, "the power of the Highest", and not of any man's seed. [L4] This conclusion rests on the layers below.

## 1. The source of the conception is stated

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

[L2] The Greek is *ek pneumatos hagiou*, "out of the Holy Spirit". The preposition *ek* (out of, from) names the source. Matthew places that source before the couple "came together" (*sunelthein*, to come together as husband and wife).

[L3] Matthew 1:20: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." Here the participle *gennēthen* (that which is begotten or conceived) is again followed by *ek pneumatos hagiou*.

[L3] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

[L2] *Episkiazō* (to overshadow) is the word for the Highest's power acting on her. *Dio kai* ("therefore also") makes the title "Son of God" follow from this manner of conception.

[L4] Two witnesses, Matthew and Luke, are footed on one lexical ground (*ek*, the source) and one cross-reference. Together they give the source of the conception as the Holy Ghost, and the child "born of thee", of Mary. No second source is given.

## 2. Mary was a virgin who knew no man

[L1] Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph... and the virgin's name was Mary."

[L1] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

[L2] *Ginōskō* (to know) here is the idiom of marital knowledge. *Andra* (man, male) is the word Mary uses. She names the very thing that would ordinarily make a father, and she says it has not happened.

[L3] Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son." The Greek is *parthenos*, virgin.

[L3] Isaiah 7:14, which Matthew quotes: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son." [L2] The Hebrew behind the KJV's "virgin" is *'almah* (H5959), a maiden.

[L3] Genesis 24:43 uses the same *'almah* for Rebekah, whom Genesis 24:16 calls "a virgin, neither had any man known her."

[L4] The word the KJV renders "virgin" in Isaiah 7:14 is the same word it renders "virgin" for Rebekah. Her virginity is stated in Genesis 24:16 with the clause "neither had any man known her". [L4] Matthew 1:23 puts the sign in the same terms: virgin, conceiving, bearing a son. Mary's own words in Luke 1:34 confirm that she was a virgin who knew no man.

## 3. Matthew breaks the genealogy's pattern of begetting

[L1] Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob."

[L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

[L2] Throughout the genealogy the verb is *egennēsen* (begat), active, with a father as subject. In verse 16 it stops. The verb becomes *egennēthē* (was born), passive, and the relative pronoun *hēs* ("of whom") is feminine singular. The relative points to Mary alone, not to Joseph.

[L3] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph." [L2] *Enomizeto* (was supposed, was reckoned) marks the sonship as an opinion held by others.

[L4] Matthew keeps the verb "begat" for every male line and drops it exactly where Joseph and Jesus are named. Matthew 1:16 therefore does not make Joseph the begetter. The feminine "of whom" has a single referent, and Luke 3:23 says plainly that the sonship was "supposed".

## 4. Joseph's role is husband, not begetter

[L1] Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man... was minded to put her away privily."

[L1] Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife."

[L1] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."

[L2] *Ouk eginōsken* (he knew her not) is the same verb *ginōskō* that Mary used in Luke 1:34. It is stated of Joseph up to the birth.

[L4] Matthew 1:19 and 1:20 together show Joseph's reaction. He was a just man who thought of putting her away, and he needed an angel to tell him not to fear. Matthew 1:25 then states that he did not know her until she gave birth.

## 5. Christ is nonetheless truly of woman and of flesh

[L1] Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law."

[L2] *Ginomai* (made, become) used with *ek gunaikos* (out of a woman) gives the human source as the woman.

[L3] Genesis 3:15: "between thy seed and her seed." The seed is called *zera'* (H2233), seed, and it is "her" seed, not a man's.

[L3] Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me."

[L4] Scripture presents the human nature as taken from the woman, and the body as one God prepared. The Father in view is God, whose Son is conceived by the Holy Ghost. A man did not beget him.

## 6. The "son of Joseph" sayings

[L1] John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" These are the words of the unbelieving Jews, and they are said as a question.

[L3] Luke 3:23 reports the same belief with the qualifier "as was supposed". [L2] *Enomizeto* is the word that carries it.

[L4] John 6:42 reports what the crowd believed. Luke 3:23, with Matthew 1:18-25, supplies the record's own account.

## DECLARED CHAIN

1. The conception of Jesus is stated to be "of the Holy Ghost": Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 [L1], *ek pneumatos hagiou* (out of the Holy Spirit) [L2], Luke 1:35 "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee... therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God" [L3].
2. Mary was a virgin who knew no man when she conceived: Luke 1:34 "seeing I know not a man" [L1], *ginōskō* (to know, in the marital sense) [L2], Matthew 1:23 and Isaiah 7:14 "a virgin shall conceive", with *'almah* (maiden) matched to Genesis 24:43 and 24:16 [L3].
3. Matthew 1:16 drops "begat" at Joseph and gives Mary alone as the one "of whom was born Jesus": Matthew 1:16 [L1], *egennēsen* (begat) in verse 2 against *egennēthē* (was born) with the feminine *hēs* (of whom) [L2], Luke 3:23 "as was supposed the son of Joseph" [L3].
4. Joseph was husband and not begetter: Matthew 1:25 "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" [L1], *ouk eginōsken* (he knew her not) [L2], Matthew 1:19-20 [L3].
5. The "son of Joseph" sayings record belief, not parentage: John 6:42 [L1], *enomizeto* (was supposed) in Luke 3:23 [L2], Matthew 1:18-25 [L3].
6. Christ had no human biological father: he was conceived of the Holy Ghost in a virgin and is called the Son of God for that reason (Luke 1:35 [L1], *dio kai* (therefore also) [L2], Galatians 4:4 "made of a woman" [L3]).

# Closing Challenge: Did Christ Have a Biological Father?

**Position.** Yes. The defender's keystone, D6, now rests on one new bridge from the link round: that "the seed of David" came "in being made of the woman." Each witness below carries its layers and answers the bridge from the text. The links are taken in order of weight.

---

## 1. LINK D6: the channel of the seed

**The defender's bridge.** It sets Romans 1:3 beside Galatians 4:4 because both use *ginomai* with *ek*.

[L1] Romans 1:3: "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;"

[L2] The source noun is *sperma* (G4690): "something sown, i.e. seed (including the male 'sperm'); by implication, offspring." The verb is *ginomai* (G1096): "to become (come into being), used with great latitude." The verb is shared. The source nouns differ: *sperma* in Romans 1:3 and *gynē* in Galatians 4:4.

[L3] Job 14:1: "Man that is born of a woman is of few days, and full of trouble. [few...: Heb. short of days]"

[L3] Matthew 11:11: "Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist." It stands with Luke 1:13: "Fear not, Zacharias ... thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son."

[L4] The defender granted in the link round that "born of women" and "her seed" sit beside a named father (Luke 1:13; Genesis 4:25). "Made of a woman" belongs to the same family of phrases as Job 14:1. Romans 1:3 gives the seed-word, *sperma*, whose lexicon sense is the male seed. So the two clauses name two sources: the seed (Romans 1:3) and the mother (Galatians 4:4). Neither is a channel for the other.

**The defender's "loins at any distance."**

[L1] Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him."

[L3] Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat Judas and his brethren;"

[L2] *Osphys* (G3751): "internally (by extension) procreative power."

[L4] Levi was in Abraham's loins across generations, and Matthew 1:2 shows the path: father begat son, three times. A remote loins-descent is a chain of begetting fathers. Acts 2:30's "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" therefore runs down such a chain. The chain the Gospels draw ends at "Joseph the husband of Mary" (Matthew 1:16), "of the house and lineage of David" (Luke 2:4). It fits my first link.

**The defender's answer on Hebrews 7:14.** The defender said the descent is "evident" because the pedigree is published.

[L1] Hebrews 7:14: "For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."

[L3] Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers."

[L2] "Declared their pedigrees" is *yalad* (H3205): "to bear young; causatively, to beget; ... specifically, to show lineage; ... declare pedigrees." The registry verb is the begetting verb.

[L3] Ezra 2:61-62: "which took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name: ... therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood. [were they...: Heb. they were polluted from the priesthood]"

[L4] The law's pedigree is declared with the begetting verb, by the fathers' house (Numbers 1:18). Ezra 2:61-62 puts out a house reckoned by the wife's name. The defender routes the flesh through Mary, and the house the rows give her is a kinship with "thy cousin Elisabeth" (Luke 1:36), who is "of the daughters of Aaron" (Luke 1:5). Hebrews 7:14's "evident ... out of Juda" fits the named father's house: Joseph, "of the house of David" (Luke 1:27).

## 2. LINK D6: the title

**The defender's own division of Romans 1:3-4.** It places the Davidic seed under "flesh" and the title under "the spirit of holiness."

[L1] Romans 1:4: "And declared to be the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead: [declared: Gr. determined]"

[L2] *Horizō* (G3724): "to mark out or bound ... appoint, decree."

[L3] 1 Chronicles 28:6: "Solomon thy son, he shall build my house and my courts: for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father."

[L4] By the defender's own division, the flesh belongs to "the seed of David" and the title to the spirit, appointed "by the resurrection." That is the Solomon pattern: David's son in the flesh, and God's son by appointment, in one verse. So the title stands apart from any begetting of the flesh.

**The defender's *dio kai*.**

[L1] Luke 1:32: "and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David."

[L1] Luke 1:35: "therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

[L2] Both verses carry *kaleō* (G2564), "to call," in "shall be called." The *dio kai* ("therefore") in v.35 connects back to v.32, and does not point forward to biological divine paternity.

[L4] Verse 32 gives the title together with the throne of David. Verse 35 restates the same calling. The result clause of v.35 is a calling, and the conception verb stands in v.31, "thou shalt conceive in thy womb."

**The defender's John 3:16.**

[L3] Hebrews 11:17: "offered up Isaac: and he that had received the promises offered up his only begotten."

[L4] "Only begotten" is said of Isaac, whose father, Abraham, is the one offering him. So the word names the unique and beloved son, and it stands beside a fleshly father.

**Psalm 2:7.** "Thou art my Son; this day have I begotten thee" is applied at its three New Testament occasions:
- the resurrection, Acts 13:33: "in that he hath raised up Jesus again";
- the priesthood, Hebrews 5:5: "to be made an high priest";
- with 2 Samuel 7:14, Hebrews 1:5: "I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son."

The defender granted these. They fit the covenant title.

## 3. LINK D1: "of the Holy Ghost"

**The defender's grant.** The defender granted that the Spirit's verbs mean "power given (Acts 1:8)" and "a cloud's presence (Luke 9:34)."

[L1] Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"

[L2] *Gennaō* (G1080): "to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother); figuratively, to regenerate."

[L3] 1 John 5:1: "every one that loveth him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him."

[L4] God is called the one "that begat" believers who have fleshly fathers (1 John 5:1). The lexicon gives *gennaō* a figurative sense, "to regenerate." In Matthew 1:20, "of the Holy Ghost" stands in the same sentence as "Joseph, thou son of David" and "Mary thy wife." So the row names the covenant origin together with the house of the named man.

## 4. LINKS D2 and D4: the timing rows and the union

**The defender's charge.** It says the order "leaves no moment for a husband."

[L1] Luke 2:5: "To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child."

[L3] Deuteronomy 22:24: "because he hath humbled his neighbour's wife." The betrothed is a wife.

[L3] Matthew 1:24: "and took unto him his wife."

[L2] Matthew 1:18's "came together" is *synerchomai* (G4905), "to come together." Matthew sets its content at 1:24, the taking into his house.

[L4] Luke names her "his espoused wife, being great with child" (Luke 2:5). The pregnancy stands inside the espousal, and in the espousal the law calls her a wife (Deuteronomy 22:24). The canon's stated means of begetting is a husband knowing his wife: "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived" (Genesis 4:1). "Till" in Matthew 1:25 bounds the abstinence to the pregnancy after the taking (Matthew 1:24). On these rows, Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins (section 1).

## 5. LINKS D3 and D5: the father named

**The defender's Luke 2:49.**

[L1] Luke 2:48: "behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."

[L3] 1 Chronicles 28:6: "Solomon thy son ... I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father."

[L4] Two fathers are named of one son in a single verse of 1 Chronicles 28:6. So "my Father's business" (Luke 2:49) stands beside Mary's "thy father" (Luke 2:48) as the covenant Father beside the house-father. After Luke 2:50 the narrator keeps "his parents" (Luke 2:41) and "Joseph and his mother" (Luke 2:43).

**The defender's naming answer.**

[L1] Luke 1:62-63: "they made signs to his father, how he would have him called. And he asked for a writing table, and wrote, saying, His name is John."

[L4] The mother spoke the name at Luke 1:60. The people then took the matter to the father, and his writing settled it (Luke 1:62-63). Matthew 1:25's "he called his name JESUS" is Joseph's act of the same kind.

**LINK 1: SUPPORTED**

*Premise:* "So the two clauses name two sources: the seed (Romans 1:3) and the mother (Galatians 4:4)."

- [L1] Galatians 4:4: "But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law,"

- [L3] Matthew 11:11: "Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist." Luke 1:13: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John."

- [L4] John is "born of women" (Matthew 11:11), and the same man is the son Elisabeth bears to Zacharias (Luke 1:13).

- Galatians 4:4 gives the mother.
- Romans 1:3 gives the seed of David, a man, *kata sarka* ("according to the flesh," the means of kindred).
- The two clauses fit as mother and seed, as they do in John.

**Answers to the presses**

MEANS [CR3] P1.1: "the same verb "made" stands in both clauses, so each gives what the one Son was made of"

MEANS [CR3] P1.2: "the woman is the stated source of the making of the Son"

MEANS [CR3] P1.3: "seed is said of the woman, so *sperma* is not only male"

# Opening: Christ had no biological father

**Position [L4]:** The KJV presents Jesus as conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost, without a man's seed. Joseph was his husband-of-his-mother and his supposed father, not his begetter. Every step below is footed in the KJV text.

---

## 1. The conception is "of the Holy Ghost"

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** The Greek behind "of the Holy Ghost" is *ek pneumatos hagiou*, "out of the Holy Spirit." The preposition *ek* (G1537) marks source or origin. The word behind "conceived" is *gennēthen* (G1080, *gennaō*), "begotten, brought into being." Matthew 1:20 therefore names the source of what was begotten in her as the Holy Spirit.

**[L3]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." *Ek sou* ("of thee") puts the child's human origin in Mary. "Therefore" (*dio*, "for which reason") ties the title "Son of God" to this conception.

**[L4]** Two accounts name the Holy Ghost as the source of the conception. Matthew 1:18 places it "before they came together," and Luke 1:35 names the Highest's power as the agent. Together these leave no place for a human begetter.

---

## 2. Mary was a virgin who had not known a man

**[L1]** Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph... and the virgin's name was Mary."

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

**[L2]** *Ginōskō* (G1097) means "to know," and in these verses it is the word for sexual knowledge. In Luke 1:34 the present tense, "I know not," states her condition at the time of the announcement.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." The same verb is used here of Joseph, and he did not know her until she had brought forth.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:23, quoting Isaiah: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son." The source passage is Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."

**[L2]** The Hebrew behind "virgin" in Isaiah 7:14 is *'almah* (H5959). The KJV renders it "virgin," and I rest on the KJV's rendering.

**[L3]** The same word stands in Genesis 24:43: "when the virgin cometh forth to draw water." That verse speaks of Rebekah, of whom Genesis 24:16 says "a virgin, neither had any man known her."

**[L4]** The angel's announcement answers a question about a woman who had known no man. Matthew 1:23 applies Isaiah 7:14 to this birth. Since the KJV renders the Hebrew as "virgin" and the Greek of Matthew 1:23 as "virgin," the conception is presented as one with no man's act in it.

---

## 3. Joseph is "supposed" father and "husband of Mary"

**[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."

**[L2]** The Greek *enomizeto* (G3543, *nomizō*) means "was thought, was reckoned by custom or opinion." It is a word about what people supposed, which may differ from the fact.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** The relative pronoun *hēs* ("of whom") is feminine singular, so it refers to Mary, not to Joseph. Matthew 1:2–15 runs "begat... begat..." but at the end of the line the pattern breaks. Joseph "begat" no one. Joseph is "the husband of Mary," and Jesus is "born" of her.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." Matthew 1:20 and 1:24 show that he received a command and then obeyed it: "Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife."

**[L4]** Joseph's reaction in Matthew 1:19 shows he knew the child was not his. Matthew 1:20 corrects his fear by naming the Holy Ghost as the source. Luke 3:23 labels Joseph's fatherhood "supposed" (*enomizeto*), and the break in the "begat" pattern in Matthew 1:16 confirms that Joseph did not beget Jesus.

---

## 4. His flesh came from the woman alone

**[L1]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law."

**[L2]** *Genomenon ek gynaikos* is "made out of a woman." Only the woman is named as the source.

**[L3]** Genesis 3:15: "between thy seed and her seed." The promised deliverer is called "her seed," and *zera'* (H2233) is "seed." The woman is named as the source, and no man's seed is mentioned.

**[L3]** Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me." The body is prepared by God and received through Mary.

**[L4]** Genesis 3:15 names "her seed," Galatians 4:4 says "made of a woman," and Hebrews 10:5 says God prepared the body. On these three, Jesus is presented as truly human, taking his flesh from his mother, with no human father's contribution.

---

## 5. Answering the likely presses

- **John 6:42:** "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" **[L1]** This is what the crowd says, and **[L3]** Luke 3:23 labels that same belief "as was supposed."
- **Luke 2:48:** "Thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." **[L1]** Mary speaks of Joseph's role as the one who stood as his father. **[L3]** In the next verse the child answers, "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" (Luke 2:49), pointing to a different Father.
- **Romans 1:3 and Acts 2:30:** "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." **[L2]** The Greek *genomenou* is the same "made" as in Galatians 4:4, **[L3]** "made of a woman." **[L4]** The line of David reaches the child through his mother, and Luke 3:23 shows Joseph's place in the line to be "supposed."

---

## DECLARED CHAIN -- the links your case stands on

1. The conception is of the Holy Ghost, not of man. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:18, 1:20; [L2] *ek pneumatos hagiou* ("out of the Holy Spirit") with *gennēthen* ("begotten"); [L3] Luke 1:35 "that holy thing which shall be born of thee."
2. Mary was a virgin who knew no man at the conception. Footing: [L1] Luke 1:34 "I know not a man"; [L2] *ginōskō* ("to know," sexual knowledge) and *'almah* in Isaiah 7:14 rendered "virgin"; [L3] Matthew 1:25 "knew her not till she had brought forth," Genesis 24:43.
3. Joseph is Mary's husband and the child's supposed father, not his begetter. Footing: [L1] Luke 3:23 "as was supposed"; [L2] *enomizeto* ("was reckoned") and feminine *hēs* ("of whom") in Matthew 1:16; [L3] Matthew 1:19, 1:24.
4. Jesus took his human flesh from a woman alone. Footing: [L1] Galatians 4:4 "made of a woman"; [L2] *ek gynaikos* ("out of a woman") and *zera'* ("seed") in Genesis 3:15; [L3] Genesis 3:15 "her seed," Hebrews 10:5 "a body hast thou prepared me."
5. Therefore Christ had no biological father. Footing: [L4] from links 1 to 4, resting on [L1] Matthew 1:20, Luke 1:35 and Galatians 4:4, with [L2] *ek pneumatos hagiou* and *ek gynaikos* ("out of the Holy Spirit," "out of a woman"), and [L3] Luke 3:23 and Matthew 1:16.

# OPENING: Christ had no biological father

**Definition.** A biological father is a man who begets a child by his own seed. I defend this: the KJV shows Christ was conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost with no human male begetting. Joseph was his father only by legal reckoning and common supposition.

## 1. The conception is "of the Holy Ghost," not of a man

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** The Greek behind "conceived" in Matthew 1:20 is *gennēthen* (from *gennaō*, G1080), "to beget, to bring into being." The same verb family runs through the genealogy's "begat" (*egennēsen*). Matthew 1:20 uses it for the very act that the genealogy assigns to each father, and assigns that act to the Holy Ghost ("of" = *ek*, "out of").

**[L3]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." The Greek *dio kai* ("therefore also") ties the child's identity to the cause named, the Holy Ghost's coming and the Highest's power.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:20 assigns the *gennēthen* of the child to the Holy Ghost [L1, L2]. Luke 1:35 names that same agent as the sole cause, and "therefore also" makes the cause explanatory [L3]. So no male begetting by Joseph or any other man is in the account. The child's origin is attributed wholly to divine power acting on Mary.

# Opening: Christ had no human biological father

**Position.** "Biological father" means the man whose seed begets the child. On the KJV text, Jesus Christ had none. Mary conceived of the Holy Ghost while a virgin, and Joseph is called the child's father only in popular supposition.

## 1. The source of the conception is the Holy Ghost, not a man

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** The Greek is *ek pneumatos hagiou*. *Ek* (G1537) means "out of, from the source of." It names the origin of the pregnancy as the Holy Spirit.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** "Conceived" is *gennēthen* (G1080, *gennaō*), "begotten, generated." The same verb is used for the fathers' part in the genealogy: "Abraham begat Isaac" (Matthew 1:2). Matthew 1:20 says the begetting in Mary is "of the Holy Ghost."

**[L3]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." The "therefore" (*dio*, G1352, "for which reason") makes the Holy Ghost's coming and the Highest's overshadowing the cause of the child's being called the Son of God.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35 name the Holy Ghost as the begetting source, and Matthew 1:2 shows *gennaō* is the word for a father's begetting. So no man's begetting occurred in Mary. These two footings carry the inference.

## 2. Mary was a virgin and had not known a man

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

**[L2]** "Know" is *ginōskō* (G1097), used in Scripture for marital knowledge. Mary's question rests on her present state: she has not known a man.

**[L1]** Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph... and the virgin's name was Mary."

**[L1]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."

**[L2]** The same *ginōskō* appears again. "Till" (*heōs*, G2193, "until") marks that Joseph did not know her through the whole span up to the birth.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:23, citing Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son." In Isaiah 7:14 the KJV reads "a virgin shall conceive." The Hebrew behind "virgin" there is *ʿalmāh* (H5959). In Matthew the Greek is *parthenos* (G3933), "virgin."

**[L4]** The conception precedes any knowing of Mary by a man (Luke 1:34; Matthew 1:25), and the sign the Lord gives is a virgin conceiving (Isaiah 7:14; Matthew 1:23). So the conception had no male human contribution.

## 3. Matthew 1:16 breaks the genealogy's "begat" pattern

**[L1]** Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob."

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** Every earlier link uses *egennēsen* (G1080), "begat," with a man as subject. In verse 16 the verb changes to the passive *egennēthē*, "was born." The relative pronoun *hēs* ("of whom") is feminine singular, so it points to Mary alone, not to Joseph. "Husband" is *anēr* (G435).

**[L4]** The pattern "X begat Y" is held for every link until Joseph. For Joseph the text says only that he is the husband of Mary, "of whom" (feminine) Jesus was born. So the genealogy withholds "begat" from Joseph and gives the birth to Mary alone. This rests on Matthew 1:2 and on the feminine *hēs* in Matthew 1:16.

## 4. Joseph's fatherhood is only "supposed"

**[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."

**[L2]** "Supposed" is *enomizeto* (G3543, *nomizō*), "to be thought, reckoned by custom." It marks an opinion, not a fact.

**[L1]** John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?"

**[L3]** This is what "they said," the crowd that went on to object to his claim "I came down from heaven" (John 6:42). It is the opinion Luke 3:23 labels "supposed."

**[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."

**[L3]** Matthew 1:20 gives the reason for the angel's word to Joseph: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." Joseph did not take the child as his own begetting. The explanation had to come to him from heaven.

**[L1]** Luke 2:48-49: Mary says, "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." The child answers, "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?"

**[L4]** Mary's "thy father" is the household's address for Joseph. The child's reply redirects "Father" to another (Luke 2:49), consistent with Luke 3:23, where Joseph's fatherhood is "supposed." Two footings carry this: Luke 3:23's "supposed" and Luke 2:49's redirect.

## 5. A body prepared, not begotten by a man

**[L1]** Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me."

**[L2]** "Prepared" is *katērtisō* (G2675), "fitted, made ready." This is the language of provision, not of a man's seed.

**[L3]** Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son." Mary is the only human parent the text names.

**[L4]** The body is prepared by God (Hebrews 10:5) and carried in Mary's womb (Luke 1:31). Together with the Holy Ghost as source (Matthew 1:20), no human father's seed is named at any point in the account.

---

DECLARED CHAIN

1. The Holy Ghost is named as the source of the conception: Matthew 1:18, 1:20 ([L2] *ek*, "out of"; *gennēthen*, "begotten") with Luke 1:35 ([L3] "therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God").
2. Mary was a virgin who had not known a man, before and until the birth: Luke 1:34 ([L2] *ginōskō*, "know") with Matthew 1:25 ([L1] "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son") and Isaiah 7:14 / Matthew 1:23 ([L2] *parthenos*, "virgin").
3. Matthew 1:16 withholds "begat" from Joseph: [L1] "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus" ([L2] *egennēthē*, "was born," with feminine *hēs*, "of whom") against Matthew 1:2 ([L3] "Abraham begat Isaac").
4. Joseph's fatherhood is only popular supposition: Luke 3:23 ([L2] *enomizeto*, "was supposed") with John 6:42 and Luke 2:48-49 ([L3] the crowd's and Mary's address, and the child's reply about "my Father's business").
5. Therefore Christ had no human biological father: the conception was of the Holy Ghost in a virgin (links 1-2), Joseph is excluded from the begetting (link 3), and his fatherhood is only supposed (link 4).

DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# Opening: Christ had no biological father

**Definition.** By "biological father" I mean a man who begets the child, so that the child is generated from him. I affirm that Jesus Christ had a biological mother, Mary, and no biological human father. His conception was of the Holy Ghost.

## 1. The conception is stated as "of the Holy Ghost," not of a man

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** The Greek is *en gastri echousa ek pneumatos hagiou*. *En gastri echousa* means "having in the womb." *Ek* (G1537) means "out of," marking the source. The source of the child in her womb is named as the Holy Ghost, *pneuma hagion* (holy spirit).

**[L3]** Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The Greek *to en autē gennēthen* uses *gennaō* (G1080, "to beget, to conceive") and again *ek pneumatos hagiou*. The angel gives this as the reason Joseph should take Mary: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L4]** Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 both use *ek*, "out of," for the origin of what was conceived. Both name the Holy Ghost as that origin. Matthew 1:18 places the pregnancy "before they came together." Since the pregnancy preceded any union with Joseph, no union with him can be its source. The only source Matthew gives is the Holy Ghost, so no human father is the biological source.

## 2. Matthew's genealogy breaks its pattern at the father's place

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** The verb for every father in the list is *egennēsen* (G1080), active voice: "begat." Verse 16 changes it. The line does not say "Joseph begat Jesus." It calls Joseph "the husband of Mary" (*ton andra Marias*), and the verb becomes passive, *egennēthē*, "was born." The relative pronoun *hēs* ("of whom") is feminine singular, so the one born is born of Mary alone.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob." This is the pattern that runs through the list until verse 16.

**[L4]** The pattern in Matthew 1:2 is that a father begets the next name. Matthew 1:16 drops that formula at exactly the place where a father would be named. It also uses the feminine "of whom" instead of a male subject. The breaking of a fixed pattern, in the grammar itself, marks that Joseph did not beget Jesus.

## 3. Mary was a virgin, and she states that she knew no man

**[L1]** Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph." Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

**[L2]** The Greek is *parthenos* (G3933), "virgin." In Luke 1:34, *andra ou ginōskō* means "I know not a man." *Ginōskō* (G1097, "to know") here means conjugal knowledge. The present tense *ginōskō* describes her state at the time she asks.

**[L3]** Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son." The angel's answer in Luke 1:35 does not say "Joseph shall come to thee." It says, "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee."

**[L4]** Mary's question in Luke 1:34 asks how a conception can occur given that she knows no man. Luke 1:35 supplies a divine agent, "the Holy Ghost… the power of the Highest," where a human husband would be expected. The answer to "how" is a divine act, so the conception has no human father.

## 4. The prophecy used for the birth is a virgin conceiving

**[L1]** Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us."

**[L2]** The Greek is *parthenos*, "virgin." Matthew quotes Isaiah 7:14, where the KJV reads "a virgin shall conceive." The Hebrew behind that verse is *ʿalmāh* (H5959), a maiden of marriageable age, unmarried.

**[L3]** Isaiah 7:14: "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son." The word "sign" matters here. A birth through ordinary marital union would not be a sign.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:22 introduces the citation as fulfilled by the events he has just described: "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled." The "all this" includes the conception "of the Holy Ghost" in verse 20. So the virgin conception in the prophecy is the one Matthew narrates, and it leaves no place for a human biological father.

## 5. Joseph's conduct and the text's qualifiers confirm it

**[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."

**[L2]** The Greek *apolusai* (G630) means "to release, put away." The word shows that Joseph did not treat the pregnancy as his own. He thought of releasing her until the angel explained its origin.

**[L3]** Luke 3:23: "Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph." The Greek *hōs enomizeto* means "as was thought, supposed." Luke marks that sonship as a supposition and not a fact.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:19 shows Joseph's first response to the pregnancy, and Matthew 1:20 supplies the correction. Together they show that Joseph was not the source. Luke 3:23 explains why people called Jesus Joseph's son: they supposed it. The same sentence marks that supposition as only a supposition, so such statements as "the son of Joseph" or "thy father" do not show biological fatherhood.

## 6. Anticipating the strongest objections

**"Thy father and I have sought thee" (Luke 2:48).** **[L1]** Luke 2:48 records Mary saying this. **[L3]** Jesus answers in Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my father's business?" His reply assigns fatherhood to God. **[L2]** Luke 2:48 uses *ho patēr sou* (G3962, "father"), a word that covers a legal or guardian father as well as a begetter. **[L4]** Luke 2:48 and 2:49 together contrast the father Mary names with the Father Jesus names.

**"Until she had brought forth" (Matthew 1:25).** **[L1]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." **[L2]** *Ginōskō* (G1097) means "to know" and is the same word Mary uses in Luke 1:34. **[L3]** Matthew 1:18 puts the pregnancy "before they came together." **[L4]** Matthew 1:25 speaks of what happened up to the birth and so excludes Joseph's involvement in the conception.

## DECLARED CHAIN

1. Matthew names the source of the conception as the Holy Ghost: Matthew 1:18 ("found with child of the Holy Ghost," *ek pneumatos hagiou*, "out of the Holy Ghost") and Matthew 1:20 ("that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost," *gennēthen*, "conceived") exhibit the origin; the pregnancy came "before they came together," so no union with Joseph can be its source.
2. Matthew's genealogy breaks its "begat" pattern at Joseph: Matthew 1:16 (*egennēthē*, "was born," with feminine *hēs*, "of whom") against Matthew 1:2 ("Abraham begat Isaac") exhibits that the father formula stops before Jesus and the birth is "of" Mary alone.
3. Mary was a virgin and knew no man, and the angel names a divine agent: Luke 1:34 ("seeing I know not a man," *ginōskō*, "to know") and Luke 1:35 ("The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee") exhibit that the "how" is answered by God's act and not by a husband.
4. The birth fulfils the virgin-conception prophecy: Matthew 1:23 (*parthenos*, "virgin") and Isaiah 7:14 ("a virgin shall conceive," *ʿalmāh*, "maiden") exhibit a "sign" that would not be one if a husband had begotten the child.
5. Passages calling Joseph Jesus' father report supposition and legal relationship, not begetting: Luke 3:23 ("as was supposed," *enomizeto*, "was thought") and Matthew 1:19-20 (Joseph's intent to put her away, then the angel's correction) exhibit that "father" language about Joseph does not state the biological source.
6. Christ had no biological father; Mary was his biological mother and the Holy Ghost the source of the conception, as Matthew 1:18, 1:20, Luke 1:35 and Matthew 1:16 jointly exhibit.

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**Answers to the presses on LINK 1:**

- **Matthew 1:24** "and took unto him his wife" (*paralambanō*, G3880, to receive near). I hold the order the challenger gives: finding (1:18), the taking (1:24), then the birth (1:25). In 1:25 the not-knowing ends at "till she had brought forth", not at the taking. The conception lies before the birth, so it lies inside the not-knowing. The challenger's step "knew Mary his wife within the espousal" has no footing against "knew her not till".
- **Deuteronomy 22:24** "because he hath humbled his neighbour's wife". I grant that the betrothed is called wife. Deuteronomy 22:23 sets betrothal and lying as two acts: "If a damsel [that is] a virgin be betrothed unto an husband, and a man find her in the city, and lie with her". Luke 1:27 names Mary "a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph". The name "wife" is given to the betrothed in Deuteronomy 22:24, while 22:23 sets the lying as a separate act after the betrothal. The name therefore does not date a union.
- **Genesis 4:1** "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived". I grant the order: the knowing comes first and the conceiving follows. *Yada'* (H3045, to know) is the verb behind Matthew 1:25's "knew her not". Matthew 1:25 states "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son". By Genesis 4:1's own order the conceiving was therefore not by it.
- **Luke 1:31** "thou shalt conceive in thy womb" and **Luke 1:34** "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" Mary's words state her condition when the promise is given, and the conceiving is still to come. Luke 1:35 then states the means: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee". The answer names the Holy Ghost as the means.

In 1 John 5:1 it is said of the already-born who believe. In Matthew 1:20 it is said of "that which is conceived in her", a conceiving "in thy womb" (Luke 1:31). John 1:13 itself puts "the will of man" on the other side of "of God". It does not set a fleshly father beside "of God".
- **Matthew 1:19** "Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." The challenger's meaning is that a just husband spared her shame. That meaning leaves "publick example" without a cause.

The "for" gives the Holy Ghost as the ground for taking her. The challenger's ground, "the seed God claims as his own", is itself a claim that the child is not of Joseph.

# Opening: Christ had no biological father

**Terms.** By "biological father" I mean a male parent who begat the child through natural generation. I hold that Christ had none. His mother was a virgin, and the child was conceived by the Holy Ghost, not by Joseph or any man. [L4, resting on the verses below]

## 1. Matthew's genealogy breaks its own pattern at Joseph

[L1] Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat Judas and his brethren". [L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

[L2] The verb in the chain is *gennaō* (G1080, "to beget"), active, with a male subject each time. At Jesus it changes to the passive *egennēthē* ("was born"). The relative pronoun *hēs* ("of whom") is feminine singular, so it points to Mary alone. It is not "of whom" in the plural, and it is not "begat Jesus".

[L3] Matthew 1:16 calls Joseph "the husband of Mary", not the one who begat. The same chapter says in Matthew 1:18 that Mary was "espoused to Joseph, before they came together".

[L4] The footing is the active "begat" (Matthew 1:2) against the passive "was born" with a feminine "of whom" (Matthew 1:16, *gennaō*). Together they show that the line of begetting stops at Joseph and the child's origin is traced to Mary only.

## 2. The conception is ascribed to the Holy Ghost

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." [L2] *ek pneumatos hagiou* means "out of [the] Holy Spirit". *Ek* (G1537) marks source or origin.

[L1] Matthew 1:20: "Joseph thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." [L2] *gennēthen* is the same root, *gennaō* (G1080), in the passive. The angel uses the verb of generation and names the Holy Ghost as its source (*ek*).

[L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." [L2] *episkiazō* (G1982, "to overshadow") is the verb of divine power. [L3] The "therefore" (*dio*) ties the child's identity as Son of God to this act.

[L4] Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 name the source (*ek*) of the conception as the Holy Ghost, and Luke 1:35 gives the mechanism, "come upon" and "overshadow". Two verses name the source and a third names the means, so no natural male source is left in the account.

## 3. Mary was a virgin and Joseph "knew her not"

[L1] Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph". [L2] *parthenos* (G3933) means virgin. [L1] Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" [L2] *andra ou ginōskō* ("a man I know not") uses *ginōskō* (G1097), "to know", in the sense of marital intimacy.

[L1] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son". [L2] The same verb, *eginōsken*, is negated up to the birth.

[L1] Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel". [L3] This quotes Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel." [L2] The Hebrew behind the KJV's "virgin" there is *ʿalmāh* (H5959). Matthew applies the verse to this birth, using *parthenos* for it.

[L4] The footing is Mary's own statement of no relations with a man (Luke 1:34) and the explicit "knew her not" until the birth (Matthew 1:25). Matthew's fulfilment citation of Isaiah 7:14 (Matthew 1:23) completes it. The conception was therefore not by a man.

## 4. Verses calling Joseph "father" are answered by the text itself

[L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph". [L2] *enomizeto* (G3543, "was supposed, reckoned") is a verb of opinion, not of fact.

[L1] John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" The speakers here are the unbelieving crowd.

[L1] Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." [L3] Jesus answers in Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" He names God as his Father.

[L4] Luke 3:23 marks Joseph's fatherhood as supposed (*enomizeto*), John 6:42 reports the crowd's assumption, and Luke 2:49 gives Jesus' own correction. Together these show that "father" language for Joseph is legal or popular, not natural begetting.

## 5. The body is God's own provision

[L1] Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me". [L1] Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman". [L3] Jeremiah 31:22: "the LORD hath created a new thing in the earth, A woman shall compass a man." [L3] Genesis 3:15 speaks of "her seed", with no male named.

[L4] Hebrews 10:5 names a body prepared by God, and Galatians 4:4 names a woman as the only human source, with no human father named. Jeremiah 31:22 calls it "a new thing", which fits a conception without a man.

## DECLARED CHAIN

1. Matthew's genealogy changes from the active "begat" to the passive "was born" with a feminine "of whom", so Joseph is not the begetter. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:2, 1:16; [L2] *gennaō* (G1080, to beget), *egennēthē* (was born), *hēs* (of whom, feminine); chain given in §1.
2. The conception is explicitly of the Holy Ghost. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:18, 1:20, Luke 1:35; [L2] *ek* (out of, source), *gennēthen* (conceived), *episkiazō* (to overshadow); chain given in §2.
3. Mary was a virgin and no man had known her before the birth. Footing: [L1] Luke 1:34, Matthew 1:25; [L2] *parthenos* (virgin), *ginōskō* (to know); [L3] Isaiah 7:14, Matthew 1:23; chain given in §3.
4. Texts that call Joseph "father" are supposition or popular speech, and Jesus names God as his Father. Footing: [L1] Luke 3:23, Luke 2:48; [L2] *enomizeto* (was supposed); [L3] Luke 2:49, John 6:42; chain given in §4.
5. God prepared the body, and a woman is the only human source named. Footing: [L1] Hebrews 10:5, Galatians 4:4; [L3] Jeremiah 31:22, Genesis 3:15; chain given in §5.
6. Therefore Christ had no biological father. He was conceived of the Holy Ghost in the virgin Mary, and God is his Father. Footing: links 1 to 5, resting on [L1] Matthew 1:18, 1:20, Luke 1:35, Luke 1:34 and [L2] *ek*, *gennaō*, *parthenos*.

# OPENING: Jesus had no biological human father

**Thesis [L4].** Jesus was conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost, without a man's seed. Joseph was his legal, reputed father and not his biological one. Each section below carries its footing.

## 1. The conception is said to be "of the Holy Ghost", before any coming together

- [L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- [L2] *sunerchomai* (G4905, "to come together", used here for the union of husband and wife) stands in this verse. The pregnancy is dated *before* that union. *Ek pneumatos hagiou* means "out of the Holy Spirit", and *ek* gives the source of the conception.

- [L4] The text gives two sources for one conception, Mary's womb and the Holy Ghost. It places that conception before any union with Joseph. The chain runs from Matthew 1:18 (timing, "before they came together") through the *ek* of Matthew 1:20 (source) to the conclusion that no man's seed was the source.

## 2. Matthew's genealogy breaks its own pattern at Joseph

The relative pronoun *hēs* is feminine singular, so it can only point to Mary. Joseph is "the husband of Mary" (*ton andra Marias*), not the one who begat.
- [L3] Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob". This is the pattern the verb sets, and it is not repeated at Joseph.

**LINK 1: SUPPORTED**

*The premise: "So the evident tribe of Hebrews 7:14 fits Joseph's loins."*

**Footing**

- **[L1]** Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood."
- **[L2]** *Osphys* (G3751, "the loin... by extension procreative power") stands in Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him." The loins are named "of his father" (*patēr*, G3962, "a father").
- **[L3]** Numbers 1:2: "after their families, by the house of their fathers, with the number of [their] names, every male by their polls." Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers."
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:2: "Jacob begat Judas and his brethren." Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus."
- **[L4]** The chain runs in four steps.
  1. A tribe is declared by pedigree "by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:18).
  2. The loins that carry a man forward are "the loins of his father" (Hebrews 7:10).
  3. Matthew carries Juda's line by "begat" from Judas to Joseph (Matthew 1:2, 16).
  4. So the tribe Hebrews 7:14 calls "evident" is evident by the line that ends at Joseph, of whom the angel says "Joseph, thou son of David" (Matthew 1:20). The evident tribe fits Joseph's loins.

**Answers to the presses**

MEANS [CR3] P1.1: "loins reach descendants beyond the immediate father, so tribe-evidence does not name Joseph's seed."

- **[L1]** Hebrews 7:5: "though they come out of the loins of Abraham."

- **[L4]** The far reach of Abraham's loins comes down step by step through fathers: Abraham, then Isaac, then Jacob, then Levi, each one "in the loins of his father" (Hebrews 7:10). So the reach of Hebrews 7:5 travels the fathers' line, and "by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:2) is the register that makes such a tribe evident. The far reach is carried by the father at each step. Matthew 1:2-16 names each step down to Joseph. It fits the link.

MEANS [CR3] P1.2: "Joseph's begetter is named as Jacob, and Joseph's own title is "husband of Mary"."

The title "husband of Mary" is the title of the man Mary calls "thy father" (Luke 2:48). So the line of Juda arrives at the husband, and the husband is called father. It fits the link.

  1. The promise requires seed going out of a man's body, "according to the flesh" (Acts 2:30; 2 Samuel 7:12).

MEANS [CR3] P2.2: "Joseph's knowing her is set after the birth."

So the *heōs* bounds the abstaining to the pregnancy after the taking, and the knowing that begets falls before the finding, within the espousal. It fits the link.

DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# OPENING: Jesus Christ had no biological father

**Position.** By "biological father" I mean the man whose seed begets the child. I hold that the KJV gives Jesus Christ a mother, Mary, and names the Holy Ghost, not a man, as the source of his conception. Joseph is his reckoned father in the household and in the genealogy, and he is not the begetter. [L4] Each step below is footed on at least two lower layers.

---

## 1. The genealogy breaks its own pattern at the last link

[L1] Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat Judas and his brethren."

[L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

[L2] In Matthew 1:2 the verb is *egennēsen* (G1080, gennaō, "begat", active voice, the man as agent). In Matthew 1:16 the last verb is *egennēthē* (the same root, passive voice, "was born"). The relative pronoun *hēs* ("of whom") is feminine singular, so it points back to Mary and not to Joseph. Joseph is called *anēr* (G435, "husband"), not the one who begat.

[L3] Matthew 1:20 supports this. The angel calls Joseph "thou son of David" and tells him to "take unto thee Mary thy wife". The command is to take her (*paralabein*, "to take to oneself"). It is not a command to acknowledge a child he had begotten.

[L4] The chain: the active "begat" runs through every earlier link (L1, Matthew 1:2). In the last link the verb turns passive and the relative pronoun turns feminine (L1 Matthew 1:16, L2 *egennēthē* and *hēs*). So the text itself carries the line of begetting to Joseph and then passes to Mary as the one of whom Jesus was born.

## 2. Mary was a virgin when she conceived

[L1] Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary."

[L2] *Parthenos* (G3933) means "virgin".

[L1] Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

[L2] *Ginōskō* (G1097, "to know") is the verb of sexual knowledge.

[L3] Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain". Here "knew" is followed by conception, so Mary's "I know not a man" states that no conception by a man has taken place.

[L1] Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us."

[L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."

[L2] The Hebrew word behind "virgin" in Isaiah 7:14 is *ʿalmāh* (H5959). [L3] Genesis 24:16 says of Rebekah: "a virgin, neither had any man known her". Genesis 24:43 then uses the same *ʿalmāh* of her: "when the virgin cometh forth to draw water". So the KJV uses this word for a woman no man has known.

[L4] Matthew 1:22 says "all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet", and then quotes Isaiah 7:14. Luke 1:27 and Luke 1:34 show Mary as a virgin who has not known a man. The conception that follows is therefore not a conception by a man.

## 3. The stated source of the conception is the Holy Ghost

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

[L2] "Of" is *ek* (G1537, "out of", the source). The phrase is *ek pneumatos hagiou*, "out of Holy Spirit".

[L1] Matthew 1:20: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

[L2] "Conceived" is *gennēthen* (from G1080, "begotten"). The verse says that what has been begotten in her is *ek pneumatos hagiou* ("out of the Holy Spirit"). The word for begetting is the one Matthew 1:2 uses for a man's begetting, and here the source of it is the Holy Ghost.

[L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

[L2] *Dio* ("for which cause") ties the title "Son of God" to the Holy Ghost's coming. *Ek sou* ("out of thee") names Mary as the one from whom he is born.

[L3] Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb". Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me". Both agree that the body of Jesus is prepared and conceived in the mother.

[L4] Matthew 1:20 gives the begetting-word (L2) with its source (L1, "of the Holy Ghost"). Luke 1:35 gives the cause (L2 *dio*, "for which cause") and the instrument (L1, "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee"). The Holy Ghost is stated as the source, and no man is named in that place.

## 4. Joseph is father by reckoning, not by begetting

[L1] Luke 3:23: "And Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph".

[L2] *Enomizeto* (G3543, "was reckoned, was supposed") is the word behind "as was supposed". It marks a reckoning by others and does not state a begetting.

[L1] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."

[L2] *Ginōskō* ("to know") is again the sexual verb. [L3] Matthew 1:20 and Matthew 1:18 supply the sequence. She was found with child "before they came together" (Matthew 1:18), and Joseph did not know her until she had brought forth.

[L1] Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."

[L1] Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?"

[L2] *Patēr* (G3962, "father") covers the man who raises and the man who begets. In Luke 2:49 Jesus answers Mary's "thy father" with "my Father's business" (*en tois tou patros mou*, "in the things of my Father"). He points to a different Father than the one Mary named.

[L3] Matthew 1:19 shows Joseph's conduct before the angel speaks: "Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily". Matthew 1:20 then has the angel give the reason for taking her: what is conceived in her "is of the Holy Ghost".

[L4] Luke 3:23 says his fatherhood by Joseph was "supposed" (L1, L2 *enomizeto*). Matthew 1:25 says Joseph did not know Mary until the birth (L1, L2 *ginōskō*, L3 Genesis 4:1). Luke 2:48–49 sets Mary's "thy father" beside Jesus's "my Father's business" (L1, L3). The word "father" in Luke 2:48 therefore names Joseph's place in the household and does not name the begetter.

## 5. The conclusion

[L4] Matthew 1:16 turns from "begat" to "of whom was born" (§1). Mary is a virgin who has not known a man (§2). The begetting is "of the Holy Ghost" (§3). Joseph's fatherhood is "as was supposed" (§4). Together these four steps support the answer that Jesus Christ had no human biological father.

---

## DECLARED CHAIN -- the links your case stands on

1. Matthew 1:16 breaks the genealogy's "begat" pattern: *egennēsen* (begat, active) in Matthew 1:2 becomes *egennēthē* (was born, passive) with the feminine *hēs* ("of whom") in Matthew 1:16, so Joseph is "the husband of Mary" and Mary is the one of whom Jesus was born. [L1 Matthew 1:2, 1:16; L2 *egennēsen*, *egennēthē*, *hēs*; L3 Matthew 1:20]
2. Mary was a virgin who had not known a man when she conceived. [L1 Luke 1:27, 1:34, Matthew 1:23; L2 *parthenos* (virgin), *ginōskō* (to know), *ʿalmāh* (H5959); L3 Genesis 4:1, 24:16, 24:43]

# Opening: Christ had no human biological father

**Position.** The KJV says Jesus was conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost, and that no man begot him. Joseph was her husband and was only supposed to be the father. Jesus is called "the Son of God" and calls God "my father". The KJV gives Jesus a mother and no human begetter.

## 1. Matthew's genealogy changes its pattern at the end

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** Each earlier name in the line uses *gennaō* (G1080, "to beget, to father"), in the active form *egennēsen*, "begat". The last link reads *ex hēs egennēthē Iēsous*, "out of whom was born Jesus". The relative pronoun *hēs* is feminine singular, so it can only refer to Mary and not to Joseph. Joseph is named *ton andra Marias*, "the husband of Mary" (*anēr*, G435, "man, husband"). He is not named as the one who begat.

**[L3]** Luke 1:27 places Mary and Joseph before any union: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph." Here *parthenos* (G3933) means "virgin".

**[L4]** The genealogy repeats "begat" down the line. At the last step it moves from the active "begat" to the passive "was born", and from Joseph to Mary as the source. Joseph is called husband, not begetter. This rests on the verb change in [L2] and on Luke 1:27 [L3]. The line of Matthew 1:16 runs to Joseph by begetting and to Jesus through Mary by birth.

# OPENING: Christ had no human biological father

**Position.** The standard reading is that Christ was conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost, with no human father. Joseph was husband and legal guardian, and the people only supposed him to be the father. I argue this from the 1611 KJV alone.

---

## I. Matthew's genealogy stops begetting at Joseph

**[L1] Matthew 1:2:** "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat Judas and his brethren."

**[L1] Matthew 1:16:** "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** The verb behind "begat" is ἐγέννησεν (egennēsen, "begat, fathered"). It runs through the whole list. In verse 16 it is not used of Joseph and Jesus. The text names Joseph as "the husband" (ἀνήρ, anēr, "husband, man") of Mary. The relative pronoun in "of whom" is ἐξ ἧς (ex hēs, "out of whom"), and it is feminine singular. It points to Mary alone, not to Joseph.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:2 sets the pattern "X begat Y", and Matthew 1:16 deliberately breaks it. The "begat" chain runs to Joseph and ends. Jesus is "born" out of the feminine "whom". The break is the evangelist's own marking of who did and did not beget.

---

## II. The stated source of the conception is the Holy Ghost, not a man

**[L1] Matthew 1:18:** "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L1] Matthew 1:20:** "…fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** "Of the Holy Ghost" is ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου (ek pneumatos hagiou, "out of the Holy Spirit"). The preposition ἐκ (ek, "out of, from") marks the origin. The text says what is conceived in her comes out of the Holy Ghost.

**[L3] Luke 1:35:** "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** "Of thee" is ἐκ σοῦ (ek sou, "out of you"). Her alone is named as the human source. "Therefore" is διό (dio, "for which reason"). The title "Son of God" is tied to this conception.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 name the Holy Ghost as the origin ([L1] with [L2] ek). Luke 1:35 names Mary as the only human source ([L3] with [L2] ek sou). Together they leave no place for a human begetter.

---

## III. Mary was a virgin, and no man had known her

**[L1] Luke 1:34:** "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

**[L2]** "Know" is γινώσκω (ginōskō), used here as the Hebrew idiom for marital knowledge. "A man" is ἄνδρα (andra, "a male person, a husband"). Mary affirms that she has had no such relation with any man.

**[L3] Matthew 1:25:** "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."

**[L3] Luke 1:27:** "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph…"

**[L2]** The word behind "virgin" in Luke 1:27 and Matthew 1:23 is παρθένος (parthenos, "virgin"). The same Greek ginōskō ("know") appears in Matthew 1:25 for Joseph. He did not know her until she had brought forth.

**[L3] Isaiah 7:14:** "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."

**[L3] Matthew 1:23:** "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us."

**[L2]** The Hebrew word standing behind the KJV's "virgin" in Isaiah 7:14 is הָעַלְמָה (ha-ʿalmāh, H5959). Matthew 1:23 quotes the verse and renders it with parthenos.

**[L4]** The conception is placed before Joseph and Mary "came together" (Matthew 1:18 [L1]). Mary denies knowing any man (Luke 1:34 [L1], with [L2] ginōskō). Matthew 1:23 applies Isaiah 7:14 to this birth ([L3]). So no human male took part in the conception.

---

## IV. Joseph is the supposed father, not the begetter

**[L1] Luke 3:23:** "And Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."

**[L2]** "As was supposed" is ἐνομίζετο (enomizeto, "was reckoned, was thought"). It is a belief held by others. It does not state a fact about begetting.

**[L3] Matthew 1:19:** "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."

**[L3] Luke 2:48–49:** "Behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing. And he said unto them, How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?"

**[L3] John 6:42:** "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?"

**[L4]** Luke 3:23 marks "son of Joseph" as a supposition ([L1] with [L2] enomizeto). Jesus answers Mary's "thy father" in Luke 2:49 by pointing to "my Father's business" ([L3]). The crowd's "whose father and mother we know" in John 6:42 is what people said, and Luke 3:23 labels such talk as supposition. Joseph's conduct in Matthew 1:19 is the conduct of a man who was not the father. The angel's word in Matthew 1:20 settles it for him.

---

## V. Descent from David does not require Joseph's seed

**[L1] Luke 1:32:** "…the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David."

**[L3] Luke 1:73:** "The oath which he sware to our father Abraham."

**[L2]** πατήρ (patēr, "father") is used in the New Testament of ancestors. David and Abraham are called "father" at a distance of many generations, so the word does not mean a begetter in every use.

**[L1] Romans 1:3:** "…which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh."

**[L3] Galatians 4:4:** "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman."

**[L2]** In both verses "made" is γενόμενον (genomenon, "having come to be"). In Galatians the source is ἐκ γυναικός (ek gynaikos, "out of a woman").

**[L4]** Romans 1:3 says Christ's flesh is of David's seed ([L1]). Galatians 4:4 says he came "of a woman" ([L3] with [L2] ek gynaikos). Luke 1:35 gives Mary as the only human source ([L3]). So the Davidic flesh comes through Mary. Luke 1:32 uses "father David" in the ancestral sense of Luke 1:73. Neither verse needs Joseph's seed.

---

## VI. The pattern foretold

**[L1] Hebrews 10:5:** "…a body hast thou prepared me."

**[L2]** The word for "body" is σῶμα (sōma, "body"). It is said to be "prepared", not begotten by a man.

**[L3] Genesis 3:15:** "…between thy seed and her seed."

# OPENING: Christ had no human biological father

**Term.** By "biological father" I mean a man who begets a child by his seed. My thesis is that Jesus had no such father. His conception in Mary was by the Holy Ghost, and no man begat him. The Father who sent him is God.

---

## 1. Matthew states the source of the conception

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
**[L2]** The phrase is *ek pneumatos hagiou* (ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου). *Ek* (G1537) means "out of" and marks source or origin. *En gastri echousa* (G1722, G1064, G2192) means "having in the womb." The pregnancy is dated "before they came together," and its source is the Holy Ghost.
**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
**[L2]** *To gennēthen* (G1080, *gennaō*, "begotten, conceived") with *ek pneumatos* gives the same source phrase. The angel assigns the begetting of the child to the Holy Ghost.
**[L4]** Matthew 1:18 gives the timing ("before they came together") and the source *ek pneumatos hagiou*. Matthew 1:20 repeats the source and applies it to the thing conceived in her. Together they say the conception was out of the Holy Ghost, and the text gives no second, human source.

## 2. Matthew's genealogy breaks its own pattern

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
**[L2]** In verses 2 to 15 the verb is active, *egennēsen* (G1080), "begat." Each time a man is the subject and the next man the object. In verse 16 the verb changes to the passive *egennēthē*, "was born," and the relative is *hēs* (ἧς), feminine singular, "of whom." Joseph is called *anēr* (G435), "husband," and is not the subject of "begat."
**[L3]** Compare Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob." The chain of "begat" runs unbroken to Joseph. It then does not say "Joseph begat Jesus."
**[L4]** The pattern of active "begat" ends at Joseph. Then the passive "was born" with a feminine relative names only Mary as the one of whom Jesus was born. That follows from Matthew 1:16 and the contrast with Matthew 1:2.

## 3. Luke: Mary's question, the angel's answer

**[L1]** Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph... and the virgin's name was Mary."
**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
**[L2]** *Ginōskō* (G1097) means "know," and in this idiom it means to know sexually. *Andra* (G435) is "a man, a male." Mary asks how, since she has had no relation with any man.
**[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
**[L2]** *Episkiazō* (G1982) means "overshadow." *Dio* (G1352) means "wherefore, on which account." The connection is causal: because the Holy Ghost comes and the power of the Highest overshadows, the holy thing born of her is the Son of God.
**[L3]** Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS."
**[L4]** Mary asks how it can happen without a man (Luke 1:34, *andra* = male). The answer names the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest, and it gives no man (Luke 1:35, *dio* = on that account). The angel's answer thus supplies a non-human source for the conception.

## 4. Joseph's conduct and the angel's correction

**[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
**[L2]** *Gar* (G1063) in verse 20 means "for, because." It gives the reason Joseph should not fear.
**[L4]** Joseph was minded to put Mary away (Matthew 1:19). The reason given for taking her instead is that what is in her is of the Holy Ghost (Matthew 1:20, *gar* = because). His plan to put her away shows he did not take the child to be his own, and the angel corrects him with the Holy Ghost as source.
**[L1]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
**[L2]** *Eginōsken* (G1097, imperfect) means "he was not knowing her." The tense marks continued non-relation up to the birth.
**[L4]** Matthew 1:25 keeps the conception free of any relation with Joseph through to the birth. It rests on the imperfect tense of *ginōskō* and on Matthew 1:18, "before they came together."

## 5. Prophecy: a virgin conceives

**[L1]** Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."
**[L2]** The Hebrew behind the KJV's "virgin" is *almah* (H5959). *Harah* (H2029) means "conceive."
**[L3]** Genesis 24:43 uses this same word, "when the virgin cometh forth to draw water." That is Rebekah. Genesis 24:16 says of her, "a virgin, neither had any man known her."
**[L1]** Matthew 1:22–23: "that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet... Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son."
**[L2]** The Greek is *parthenos* (G3933), "virgin."
**[L4]** Isaiah 7:14 has a virgin who conceives. Genesis 24:43 and 24:16 show the same word *almah* applied to a virgin whom no man had known. Matthew 1:22–23 applies the prophecy to the birth of Jesus and renders the word as virgin. The virgin conceiving is therefore the sign given, and it is fulfilled in Mary.

## 6. A body prepared, and the Father named

**[L1]** Hebrews 10:5: "Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me."
**[L2]** *Katartizō* (G2675) means "to fit, prepare." *Sōma* (G4983) means "body." The one who prepared the body is the one addressed, God.
**[L3]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman." The Son is sent by God, and his human making is "of a woman."
**[L4]** Hebrews 10:5 says God prepared the body, and Galatians 4:4 says God sent the Son who was made of a woman. These agree with Luke 1:35: the body in Mary came by God's act through the Holy Ghost.

## 7. Where Joseph is called father, and why that does not overturn this

**[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."
**[L2]** *Nomizō* (G3543) means "to think, suppose by custom or law." The KJV flags the sonship as supposed.
**[L1]** Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." Mary speaks here as one raising the child in the household.
**[L1]** Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?"
**[L3]** John 5:18: "said also that God was his Father."
**[L4]** Luke 3:23 marks Joseph's sonship as supposed (*nomizō*). In Luke 2:48–49 the child's own answer to "thy father" is "my Father's business," and the next verses say Joseph and Mary "understood not the saying" (Luke 2:50). John 5:18 shows the Jews understood the claim as being about God. The text distinguishes the household father from the Father who sent him.

---

## DECLARED CHAIN

1. The conception in Mary was out of the Holy Ghost, not out of a man. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:18, "found with child of the Holy Ghost," and Matthew 1:20, "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost," with [L2] *ek pneumatos hagiou* (out of the Holy Ghost) and *gennēthen* (G1080, begotten); the chain runs from the stated source to the conception.
2. Matthew's genealogy ends the line of "begat" at Joseph and says Jesus was born "of whom," Mary. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:16, "of whom was born Jesus," with [L2] *hēs* (feminine singular "of whom") and the passive *egennēthē* (was born), against [L3] Matthew 1:2, "Abraham begat Isaac," and the active pattern.
3. Mary's question and the angel's answer exclude a man and name the Holy Ghost with the power of the Highest. Footing: [L1] Luke 1:34, "seeing I know not a man," and Luke 1:35, "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee," with [L2] *andra* (a man, a male), *episkiazō* (overshadow) and *dio* (on that account), plus [L3] Matthew 1:25, "knew her not till she had brought forth."
4. Isaiah 7:14 is a virgin-conception sign, and Matthew applies it to Jesus. Footing: [L1] Isaiah 7:14, "a virgin shall conceive," with [L2] *almah* (H5959), [L3] Genesis 24:43 and 24:16 ("a virgin, neither had any man known her"), and Matthew 1:23, "a virgin shall be with child."
5. Joseph's "fatherhood" is a supposed or household one, and the Father who sent him is God. Footing: [L1] Luke 3:23, "as was supposed," with [L2] *nomizō* (suppose by custom), and [L3] Luke 2:49, "my Father's business," and Hebrews 10:5, "a body hast thou prepared me."
6. Therefore Christ had no human biological father: he was conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost, and no man begat him. Footing: links 1 to 5, resting on [L1] Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35 with [L2] *ek pneumatos hagiou* (out of the Holy Ghost) and *dio* (on that account).

# CLOSE OF THE CHALLENGE: The Seed Out of David's Loins Comes Down the House of the Fathers, and That House Is Joseph's

The defender's second round brought new rows. Each is answered below from its own words. Several of them carry a named father in the same verse.

---

## A. The answer to Hebrews 7:14, measured

### A1. "By legal reckoning, without a begetting"

**[L1]** Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."
**[L2]** *Anatetalken* (G393, to spring up, to rise) is a verb of rising out of a stock.
**[L3]** Hebrews 7:5 sets the sons of Levi in a stock: "though they come out of the loins of Abraham."

# DEFENDER'S OPENING

The reading I defend, the standard reading of the record: the man Jesus, called Christ, was conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost, and had no biological father. ## LINK 1 — The conception stands before the union of Mary and Joseph

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

The verse states time and source together: the child was found in Mary "before they came together," and the child is "of the Holy Ghost."

[L2] "they came together" — συνέρχομαι (synerchomai, G4905 — to come together; of husband and wife, the marriage union).
